common_name: Bill Bailey Pitcher Plant (Giant-Trap Bornean Nepenthes Hybrid)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or pot up nursery starts in spring into a well-draining mix of sphagnum moss and orchid bark or perlite; keep the medium moist year-round with pure distilled, reverse-osmosis, or rainwater and provide bright, above-average humidity.

directions: Grow in a well-draining mix of sphagnum moss and orchid bark or perlite in bright, filtered light with above-average humidity, watering only with distilled, reverse-osmosis, or rain water. Bill Bailey is a complex Bornean highland hybrid from Borneo Exotics prized for producing exceptionally large, broad-shouldered pitchers heavily marked in maroon-red blotching over a pale orange to cream ground color, with a wide, flared peristome that gives each pitcher a bold, showy presence. It is a vigorous climber once established, throwing both squat lower pitchers and more elongated upper pitchers as the vine matures. Provide a hanging basket or elevated position to display the pitchers, and feed occasionally with a small live or dead insect if grown indoors away from natural prey.

It climbs modestly with maturity, producing both lower and upper pitchers of differing shape. Rebecca Soper is a complex Bornean highland hybrid from Borneo Exotics, part of a series of hybrids named for individuals associated with the nursery, known for compact growth and richly colored pitchers in mottled orange-red over a cream base. It pitchers freely even on relatively young plants, making it a rewarding grower for collectors who want striking color without a huge mature footprint. Lady Pauline is a complex Bornean highland hybrid from Borneo Exotics that produces elegant, elongated funnel-shaped pitchers mottled in orange to red over a paler ground, with upper pitchers on climbing growth that are notably more slender than the rounder lower pitchers. It is a steady, vigorous climber once established and rewards patient growers with a long-lasting display of dangling traps. Provide a hanging basket or elevated position to display the pitchers, and feed occasionally with a small live or dead insect if grown indoors away from natural prey.
